claims.text: GDACS's event report for 'Flood in Sri Lanka' (event id 1104075, source GLOFAS, overall Green alert, reporting window 02 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC to 04 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC) records via its Sendai indicator feed: 8 fatalities in Sri Lanka and 4 fatalities specifically in Hatton (12 total); 3,316 people evacuated plus 3,566 more evacuated (6,882 total); 15,412 people / 1,512 households affected; 537 and 129 buildings damaged (666 total); and 21 people rescued in Gampola.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) is unchanged — the same 2-4 August 2026 reporting window, 12 confirmed deaths and 6,882 evacuated via the Sendai indicator feed; no episode 2 or newer figures have been published.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's Sendai indicator feed for event FL 1104075 was refreshed at 08:00:35 UTC today; the summed figures are unchanged at 12 fatalities (8 general + 4 in Hatton) and 6,882 evacuated (3,316 + 3,566), with 15,412 people/1,512 households affected and 666 buildings damaged. No episode 2 has been published.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: GDACS's event report for this flood event (eventid 1104075, episode 1) remains last updated 6 August 2026, with no Episode 2 issued. Death toll (12) and displaced figure (6,882) are unchanged.

description: Heavy monsoon rainfall triggered flooding and landslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands beginning around 2 August 2026, affecting Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Kegalle and Ratnapura districts, with the town of Hatton (Nuwara Eliya District) singled out for a fatal landslide. GDACS assessed the event as an overall Green alert (low humanitarian impact) for a reporting window of 2-4 August 2026, but its Sendai indicator feed records 12 confirmed deaths and about 6,882 people evacuated, alongside 15,412 people (1,512 households) affected and 666 buildings damaged. The disaster drew sustained international coverage given the region's continuing recovery from Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025), with authorities ordering school closures and military-assisted evacuations in affected districts. No allowlisted source has declared the event resolved. Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) is unchanged — the same 2-4 August 2026 reporting window, 12 confirmed deaths and 6,882 evacuated via the Sendai indicator feed; no episode 2 or newer figures have been published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) was refreshed at 08:00 UTC today but its Sendai indicator figures are unchanged — 12 confirmed deaths (8 general + 4 in Hatton) and 6,882 evacuated (3,316 + 3,566); no episode 2 has been published. Re-checked 10 August 2026: GDACS's report (episode 1) remains last updated 6 August 2026 with no newer episode issued; figures (12 deaths, 6,882 displaced) are unchanged.
